docs.title: Sampling Methods Vocabulary
docs.text:
Status: 🟡 Draft

Controlled vocabulary of sample collection methods used in environmental monitoring, developed within the PARC project (Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals). Covers active and passive air sampling, atmospheric deposition collectors, point (grab) sampling of water, sediment and soil, plant material sampling, and depth-profile sampling. Scope is currently limited to the outdoor (ambient) environment — indoor matrices (indoor air, indoor dust) and biota (e.g. fish, mussels) are not yet covered and may be added in a future version.

docs.title: Concept Information
docs.text: Notation ActiveHiVol Preferred label Active - HiVol Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/ActiveHiVol URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Active air sampling using a high-volume sampler. Air is continuously drawn by a pump through a filter and, where applicable, a sorbent medium, on which the target substances are captured. The method uses high air flow rates, typically 200 to 700 L/min (≈ 12 to 42 m³/h), allowing a large volume of air to be processed during the sampling interval and enabling determination of very low analyte concentrations. It is used mainly for monitoring persistent organic pollutants (POPs), PAHs, pesticides, and other trace contaminants in ambient air.

docs.title: Concept Information
docs.text: Notation ActiveLowVol Preferred label Active - LowVol Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/ActiveLowVol URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Active air sampling using a low-volume sampler. Air is continuously drawn by a pump through a filter or sorbent medium, on which the target substances are captured. The method uses lower air flow rates, typically 1 to 40 L/min for sorbent-based sampling, or approximately 1 to 3 m³/h (≈ 16 to 50 L/min) for standard PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅ monitoring samplers. The method is suitable for routine long-term air quality monitoring and exposure studies.

docs.title: Concept Information
docs.text: Notation BulkCollector Preferred label Bulk collector Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/BulkCollector URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Precipitation and dry deposition are collected together in a permanently open collection device. The method provides data on total (wet and dry) atmospheric deposition of the target substances.

docs.text: Notation FieldSampling Preferred label Field sampling Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/FieldSampling URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Field collection of plant material. A sample of a plant, or part of a plant, is collected at a defined location and time and represents the state of the plant matrix at the moment of sampling.

docs.title: Concept Information
docs.text: Notation Grab Preferred label Grab Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/Grab URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Point (grab) sampling of water, sediment, or soil. The sample is taken once, from a specific location and time, without combining it with other sub-samples. It represents the condition of the given matrix at the moment of sampling.

docs.text: Notation GrabFiltration Preferred label Grab + Filtration Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/GrabFiltration URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Point (grab) sampling of water or sediment, followed by filtration. After collection, the sample is filtered to separate the dissolved and solid (particulate) phases for subsequent analysis.

docs.title: Concept Information
docs.text: Notation PassiveDGT Preferred label Passive DGT Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/PassiveDGT URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Passive sampling of water, sediment, or soil using DGT (Diffusive Gradients in Thin-films). Target substances diffuse through a hydrogel layer and are accumulated on a binding resin, without the use of a pump. The method is used mainly for trace metals and other inorganic/ionic contaminants; binding gels adapted for other substance groups also exist.

docs.title: Concept Information
docs.text: Notation PassivePOCIS Preferred label Passive POCIS Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/PassivePOCIS URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Passive water sampling using a POCIS (Polar Organic Chemical Integrative Sampler). Target substances are continuously accumulated from the aquatic environment onto a sorbent medium enclosed between semipermeable membranes, without the use of a pump. The method is intended mainly for monitoring polar organic contaminants.

docs.text: Notation PassiveSPMD Preferred label Passive SPMD Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/PassiveSPMD URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Passive water sampling using a semipermeable membrane device (SPMD). Target substances diffuse from the aquatic environment through a semipermeable membrane into the accumulation medium, without the use of a pump. The method is intended mainly for long-term monitoring of hydrophobic organic contaminants.

docs.title: Concept Information
docs.text: Notation WetOnlyCollector Preferred label Wet-only collector Concept URI https://w3id.org/chemical-exposome/terms/WetOnlyCollector URI type Minted in this vocabulary Part of SamplingMethod

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: The collection device is automatically opened only during precipitation events, so only precipitation and wet deposition are collected. Dry deposition between precipitation episodes is not sampled.
